title: Executive Order 14412 of June 22, 2026: Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
date_evidence: Federal Register Vol. 91, No. 121, Thursday, June 25, 2026 ... Executive Order 14412 of June 22, 2026
key_claim: EO 14412 requires OMB guidance within 90 days directing agencies to transition all high value assets and high impact systems to post-quantum cryptography for key establishment by December 31, 2030 and for digital signatures by December 31, 2031; each agency must name a PQC migration lead within 30 days; within 180 days the FAR Council must publish a proposed rule requiring covered contractors to comply with NIST FIPS, including PQC-compliant algorithms, by December 31, 2030; within 270 days CISA must release guidance on minimum elements of a cryptographic bill of materials enabling automated assessment of cryptographic assets; sector risk management agencies must assist critical infrastructure owners with migration plans, and the State Department must encourage foreign governments to adopt NIST-standardised PQC algorithms.
frame_summary: The order frames harvest-now-decrypt-later collection as a present national security threat and converts post-quantum migration from strategy into binding deadlines enforced through agency governance and federal procurement.
notes: Primary text as published in the Federal Register (FR Doc 2026-12909). Signed 22 June 2026; published 25 June 2026.

publisher: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI)
title: BSI empfiehlt Ende klassischer asymmetrischer Verschlüsselungsverfahren (press release on TR-02102 update)
key_claim: In the annual update of its cryptographic recommendations (TR-02102) the BSI for the first time sets an end date for classical asymmetric encryption: from the end of 2031, and for highly sensitive applications from the end of 2030, these methods should no longer be used alone but combined with post-quantum cryptography in hybrid form; sole use of classical signature schemes is to end by 2035; BSI president Claudia Plattner calls the switch to post-quantum procedures 'alternativlos' (without alternative); TR-02102 is used internationally as a state-of-the-art reference and conformity is mandatory in numerous products, including those processing classified information.
frame_summary: Germany's federal cyber authority frames the end of classical encryption as settled and non-negotiable, converting migration timelines into a de facto compliance standard through TR-conformity requirements.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band) and German-language Tier 1 source satisfying the multi-language protocol; canonical European framing of binding migration dates.

publisher: Center for Cybersecurity Policy and Law
title: From Strategy to Implementation: The White House Accelerates the Federal Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
key_claim: The executive order shifts federal quantum policy from standards development and planning to implementation, building on the March 2026 Cyber Strategy, CISA's January product-categories list and NIST's draft guidance on post-quantum Personal Identity Verification credentials; Senate Armed Services Committee text for the FY2027 NDAA would require the Department of Defense to migrate to NIST-approved PQC on an accelerated schedule; a cryptographic bill of materials could become as central to supply-chain security as SBOMs, and quantum readiness is becoming part of the broader federal compliance landscape for contractors and technology providers.
frame_summary: The think-tank reads the order as the moment post-quantum migration became an operational compliance regime, with congressional, procurement and agency tracks aligning to push obligations outward through the contractor ecosystem.
notes: Tier 2 policy-institute analysis; carries the NDAA and CBOM strands.

title: New Executive Orders and Government Strategy Advance US Quantum Innovation and Mandate Post-Quantum Cryptography Transition
date_evidence: June 30, 2026 / Skadden Publication / National Security Dispatch
key_claim: The Cryptographic Order accelerates the previous 2035 PQC migration deadline to 2030 for key compliance requirements; on June 23, 2026 the Department of War released its Post Quantum Cryptography Strategy requiring all DoW systems to support PQC or be phased out by December 31, 2030 and to use PQC by December 31, 2031, noting that 'nearly every deployed military asset will be affected in some way'; the strategy extends cryptographic requirements across the defense industrial base including updates to CMMC; given the weight of federal procurement, the FAR requirement is expected to flow through the supplier ecosystem and spur PQC adoption across a broader swath of the US economy by 2030; a companion order, EO 14413, accelerates quantum innovation, export-control alignment and workforce development.
frame_summary: Counsel advises that the orders create enforceable timelines whose real reach is through procurement flow-downs, telling contractors, cloud providers and critical-infrastructure firms to treat PQC readiness as a present compliance obligation.
notes: Law-firm client alert; source for the DoW strategy detail and the 2035-to-2030 acceleration framing.

title: Quantum Security Deadlines are Here - What Happens Next?
date_evidence: The article, titled 'Quantum Security Deadlines are Here - What Happens Next?' was published on May 8, 2026, by The Quantum Insider (search-result snippet; URL dateline /2026/05/08/).
key_claim: NIST IR 8547 designates quantum-vulnerable algorithms including RSA-2048 and ECC P-256 for deprecation by 2030 and disallows them by 2035; NSA CNSA 2.0 requires new national security systems and acquisitions to support quantum-resistant cryptography from 2027, with exclusive use across covered categories phased to 2031-2033 and full quantum resistance by 2035; the EU roadmap expects member states to publish national PQC strategies, initiate cryptographic inventories and launch pilots by the end of 2026, transition critical infrastructure high-risk use cases by end-2030 and complete medium-risk migration by 2035; US federal migration costs have been estimated at $7.1 billion; recent research has reduced estimated quantum resource requirements for breaking RSA-2048 from tens of millions of qubits to under one million under certain assumptions, though these projections depend on error-correction advances still under development.
frame_summary: The trade press aggregates the converging government timetables into one message: the regulatory clocks are already running and multi-year migrations must start now, whatever the true arrival date of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.
notes: Specialist trade press; page body carries no visible dateline to plain fetch, so the date is captured from the search-result snippet per the date-capture protocol step 4(a). Part of the publication's 'Year of Quantum Security 2026' editorial initiative (partner-supported); treated as Tier 3 with that caveat.

title: World Quantum Day 2026 - The slow arrival of quantum computing (and the fast arrival of its risks)
key_claim: Practitioner views collected for World Quantum Day 2026 range from Google-linked predictions that Q-Day could arrive as early as 2029 to contrarians doubting qubit-entanglement machines will ever work as hoped; Entrust's global VP of technical solutions cites the 2026 Global State of Post-Quantum and Cryptographic Security Trends report finding that only 38% of organisations globally are currently transitioning to PQC; adversaries are already using harvest-now-decrypt-later tactics, and the shift to post-quantum cryptography has become a multi-year transformation programme.
frame_summary: The feature's own framing is the signal: hardware arrival remains slow and contested while the security and compliance risks arrive fast, leaving a large readiness gap between regulatory timetables and organisational reality.
notes: Carrier for the sourced counter-argument (timeline scepticism, low transition rates) and the 38% readiness figure.

title: The post-quantum EO is an important milestone. Now it's time to get to work
key_claim: Over two-thirds of browser traffic to Cloudflare's network is already protected with post-quantum encryption; the migration splits into post-quantum encryption (needed now against harvest-now-decrypt-later) and post-quantum authentication, whose longer dependency chain spans clients, servers, certificate authorities, certificate transparency logs, root stores and browsers; Cloudflare moved its own full post-quantum target to 2029 following research breakthroughs; the EO's contractor requirements may be its most impactful part, forcing the vendor ecosystem to ship PQC-capable products that hospitals, banks and small businesses then inherit; the company cautions that OMB guidance must define what 'transition' means to avoid downgrade attacks and warns against treating exhaustive cryptographic inventories as a prerequisite for action.
frame_summary: A vendor at the front of deployment welcomes the order, argues procurement flow-through will carry PQC to the whole economy, and pushes for implementation guidance that measures completion by disabling classical cryptography rather than merely supporting new algorithms.
notes: Vendor perspective used as directional corroboration; note the post refers to the order as EO 14409, whereas the Federal Register text (FR Doc 2026-12909) numbers it 14412 - the Federal Register is treated as authoritative.
